 : Judgment :

The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB / NH-7 /
CR / 23 / 2011-12 dated 02.02.2021 in respect of Sy. No.9/1A measuring 656.36 Sq. feets of Byatarayanapura village, Yelahanka, Bengaluru North Addl. Taluka, Bengaluru Urban District.

.2. The definite case of the petitioner is that the property bearing Sy. No.9/1A measuring 656.36 Sq.
A.P. No.87/2022 feets situated at Byatarayanapura village, Yelahanka Hobli has been acquired under Gazette notification No. S.O. No.1874(E) dated 30.07.2010.
Prior to that Preliminary Notification issued under S.O. No.3159(E) dated 09.12.2009.
Subsequently the respondent No.2/LAO has awarded a total sum of Rs.12,64,805/- as compensation for 656.36 Sq. feets of the land belongs to the petitioner.
The petitioner received the same under protest and filed an application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.8,500/- per Sq. feet as on 30.09.2011.
Accordingly, the said application taken by the respondent No. 3 for consideration.
.3. In the said petition, the respondent No.2 filed statement of objection stating that the contention urged by the petitioner are baseless and the same are made without any substance.
The petitioner has not produced any relevant documents to justify his claim for enhanced compensation and the claim of the petitioner cannot be sustained in law.
Hence, question of enhancement of compensation will not arise and the A.P. No.87/2022 claim of the petitioner is liable to be dismissed by the respondent No.2.
Accordingly, prayed to dismiss the reference.

.4. Thereafter, the Arbitrator hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR-23,
22, 21, 20,19,18,17,49, 26,24/2011-12, 37/2012-13 dated 02.02. 2021.
.5.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting up the following :
:GROUNDS:
The petitioner claims that the impugned award passed by the respondent No.3 is wholly erroneous, contrary to law, materials on record and in violation of Principles of natural justice and the same is liable to be set aside.

The petitioner claims that the Gomathi Ben vs The Project Director And General ... on 2 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118746433/
2 respondent No.3 committed a legal misconduct in not following the documents filed by the petitioner for deciding the market value.

sentences.text:
The Arbitrator failed to appreciate the fact that the respondent No.
3 has not produced any documents to justify the award passed by him.
The award dated 28.01.2011 passed by the respondent No. 2 is not in accordance with the guidance value under Section 3G(7) of NH Act.
The award amount is not at all matching with the market value for prime land of the petitioner.
The land acquired is more than value than the award amount, even the amount awarded.
The respondent No.3 enhanced just and meager compensation without taken into consideration material evidence placed before the Court, which is against probabilities of the case.
The respondent No. 3 grossly erred in considering the fact that the acquired land situated very near to Bengaluru International Airport and situated amidst the lands commercially developed.

The LAO and Arbitrator has not recorded any evidence and not considered for payment of solatium on the award amount and additional market value along with interest from the date of A.P. No.87/2022 taking possession till the date of payment.
Accordingly, prayed for reconsidering the impugned award and also alternative prayer to remand the matter to the Arbitrator for fresh consideration.

.6. The respondent No.1 and 2 filed a detailed objections claiming that the application is not maintainable either in law or on facts and the respondent No. 3 passed the award as per the guidance value produced before the Arbitrator pertaining to the year 2011.
The petitioner is attempting to mislead this Court by drawing reference to incorrect/wholly inapplicable guidance notification.
The respondent No.1 totally denied all the grounds claimed by the petitioner in the petition.

The Arbitrator/ respondent No. 3 passed the award after giving full opportunity of hearing to the petitioner by considering the material evidence on record for enhancement of compensation together with all other statutory benefits available under A.P. No.87/2022 the LA Act in accordance with law and prayed for dismissal of the petition.
.7. The petitioner along with the petition filed I.A. No. 1 under Section 34(3) of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, for condonation of delay if any filing the petition.

.8. The above application is supported with the affidavit of petitioner, wherein, it is stated that the order has not been communicated to her and when she approached the concerned authority on 17.12.2021, she came to know about the order and she immediately applied for copy of the order and he got the same on 26.05.2022.
Thereafter, filed this petition and accordingly prayed for condonation of delay if any in filing the petition.
.9. The respondent No.1 has not filed any objections to the IA.
.10. The respondents No.1 and 2 appeared before the Court through their Advocate.
The respondent No.3 did not appear before the Court and hence, the A.P. No.87/2022 respondent No.3 has been placed exparte.
The entire records in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/23/2011-12 secured from the Arbitrator.

On the basis of above, the points for consideration are as under:
1) Whether the petition filed by the petitioner is within time ?
2) Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?
3) What order or award?
.12.
Heard the arguments.

The learned advocate for the petitioner relied on judgments reported in (1) In Civil Appeal No. 7064/2019 (Arising out of SLP (C) No. 9599 of 2019) - Union of India Vs.
Tarsem Singh; (2) In No. SLP (C) No.19775/2021 (2022 LiveLaw (SC) 584) ; (3) Judgment dated 12.09.2024 of this Court in A.P. No.81/2022 - Sri. J.M. Krishnappa Vs. The Project Director and General Manager and others; (4) SLAO and another Vs. Sri. Muthaiah and another in MFA No. A.P.
No.87/2022 2930/2020; (5) Judgment dated 20.08.2022 of High Court of Bombay - NHAI and another Vs. the Additional Commissioner and others; and (6) In Suo Motu Writ petition (Civil) No.

Perused the materials on record, on that basis my findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 : In the affirmative Point No.2 : In the negative Point No.3 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS .13. POINT NO.1: Perused the I.A. No.1 along with affidavit that has been filed for condonation of delay in filing the petition, satisfied with reasons therein and the said application is not opposed by the respondent No. 1.

Accordingly, I am of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to condone A.P.
No.87/2022 the delay in filing the petition.
Accordingly the point No. 1 is held in the affirmative.
.14. POINT No.2:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note an admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The petitioner Smt. Gomathi Ben is an owner of the property bearing Sy. No.9/1A measuring to an extent of 656.36 Sq. feets of Byatarayanapura village, Yelahanka,
Bengaluru North Additional Taluka and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-7 under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 30.07.2010, that has been published in the official Gazette on 30.07.2010, is an admitted fact.
It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.12,64,805/- being the land value was disbursed to the petitioner as compensation.

.15. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the petitioner Smt. Gomathi Ben filed an application before the respondent No.3 claiming that she is entitled for compensation at the A.P. No.87/2022 rate of Rs. 8,500/- per Sq. feet as on 30.09.2011.
On basis of the said application, the respondent No.3 hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ/ARB/NH- 7/CR-23, 22, 21, 20,19,18,17,49, 26,24/2011-12, 37/2012-13 dated 02.02.2021.

The respondent No.3 Gomathi Ben vs The Project Director And General ... on 2 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118746433/
4 in its order enhanced the compensation at Rs.5,250/- per Sq. feet from Rs. 1,927/- per Sq. feet

sentences.text: and awarded additional compensation of Rs.3,323/- per Sq. feet.
.16. The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No.3 without considering the documentary evidence placed by the petitioner and also without considering the claim of the petitioner that other properties have enhanced the market value which is much higher than the compensation enhanced by the respondent No. 3.
The said claim of the petitioner is also found in the award.

On close perusal of the order passed by the respondent No. 3, it is clear that the respondent No. 3 considering the guidance value of the year 2010-11 published vide A.P. No.87/2022 notification bearing No. CVC 19/2010-11 dated 21.09.2011 enhanced the compensation, but there is no material on record to show that the petitioner has produced the alleged documents claimed by the petitioner in the petition for perusal of Arbitrator/respondent No. 3 so that the respondent No.3 has an opportunity to consider the claim of this petitioner before passing the impugned order.

.17. However, it is the definite case of petitioner that the very same Arbitrator in different cases has enhanced the market value 3 times and such enhancement of compensation not given to the petitioner though the property of the petitioner is acquired for National Highways and the said property of the petitioner was abutting to the National Highways.
.18. In support of this contention, the petitioner has produced the copy of the order passed in LAQ/ARB/NH-07/CR/01/2019-20 dated 09.01.2020.
In the said case, the LAO has enhanced the compensation 3 times of the compensation awarded by A.P. No.87/2022 LAO/ respondent No. 2.
Admittedly in the case on hand, the LAO awarded the compensation of Rs.1,927/- per Sq. feet and it is enhanced to the tune of Rs.5,250/- per Sq. feet by enhancing only Rs.3,323/- per Sq. feets.
Even it is considered, the Arbitrator considered the claim of petitioner in his order and enhanced almost 3 times.
The compensation awarded by the LAO is at Rs. 1,927/- per Sq. feet that has been enhanced to Rs. 5,250/- per Sq. feet.
The petitioner has not placed any material before the Court to show that the market value can be enhanced more than Rs. 5,250/- per Sq. feet.
Even there is no material on record to show that the market value has been enhanced for more than Rs. 5,250/- per Sq. feet.

Under such circumstance, the Court cannot find any fault in findings of the Arbitrator, as such,
certainly there is no material whatsoever on record to show to intervene with the order of Arbitrator and the Arbitrator considered all material fact and evidence placed before him while passing the order.
Accordingly, the point No.2 is held in the negative.
Point No.3:
In view of my above findings, I proceed to pass the following.
ORDER IA filed by the petitioner to condone the delay in filing the petition is allowed.
Petition filed under Section 34 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 by the petitioner is hereby dismissed.

Consequently, the impugned award passed by the respondent No.3 in case No.LAQ / ARB / NH-7 /
